P1.evidence: Setter named and referenced: 'Kim is by the way his name. Kim already gave me some ideas from where you want to go to, where you're at at the moment. But I just want to hear everything from you to make sure I really get a good picture.' Frame is the usual three parts, missing 'what's in the way' and 'what you need'. Agreement obtained ('Sounds good?' — 'Sounds good to me') and the open question ran verbatim.

P2.evidence: Age and weight both asked directly ('how old are you at the moment?' — 33; 'how much do you weigh at the moment?' — 185); height volunteered. Work covered thoroughly and usefully — the rep drew out the hydraulic tool, the 100 lb of equipment and the ladder climbing, which is exactly the input a programme should want. The health-conditions question was never asked: the throat surgery surfaced only because the setter had flagged smoking and drinking and the rep probed that instead ('he told me something about smoking and drinking. Do you mean that?'). Diet asked well including protein estimates. Sleep never asked despite the prospect volunteering that it had been the central problem of his life for a decade.

P3.evidence: Good work pinning a vague goal down. The prospect said 'I don't really have a goal' and the rep pushed until he had one — 'Well, what would you want to see in the mirror? Let's just say that.' — producing the stomach and lean-look target. The ten-year future-pace ran and produced the best answer on the call: 'you know, 45 years old, in great shape, just able to do whatever it is I feel like I want to do physically... go hiking, climbing a mountain.' But 'who else does that impact' was never asked at all, no family or relationships were explored in a 62-minute call, and there was no reflect-back.

P4.evidence: The strongest phase of the call. 'What do you feel like was missing for you that sort of didn't make it click?' produced the whole story — the colleague's three-hour sessions, the mismatch in goals, and the social bind of not wanting to refuse someone donating their time. The prospect then named the gap himself and precisely: 'I'm willing to make whatever type of dietary changes I need. It's just the guidance I need. Because if I'm left to my own devices, I'm not going to know what the hell to do.' Only the scripted 'the information isn't the problem' line is absent.

P5.evidence: The rep tried repeatedly and could not land it. He asked a version of the settle question four separate times across 00:28:20-00:31:29 and the prospect misunderstood each attempt, answering about dedication rather than consequence ('If this is the question about dedication, I don't think there's any question to be had'). The rep eventually accepted that answer and moved on. No two-year picture, no 'why not', no line in the sand. The phrasing was the problem — long, negatively framed and hypothetical.

P6.evidence: Belief question ran cleanly before the offer: 'do you feel like you're confident that we can get you to the goal where you lose the fat as a by-product of getting stronger, getting more energy?' — 'I do believe so.' The 'if you had everything you needed, is there any reason you wouldn't go all in' question never ran. The readiness check that followed was answered obliquely — 'I mean, I'm here at four in the morning' — which the rep took as a yes, and it was a reasonable read, but it is not the scripted commitment.

P11.evidence: A $100 deposit link was sent live by WhatsApp and receipt confirmed, but no payment was collected on the call — the prospect had to fetch his wallet from his car and promised to complete it within the hour, and $5,900 remains contingent on an insurance reimbursement with no date. The rep said 'let me just push a meeting real quick' and referenced Monday with Trevor but no booking was confirmed. No agreement email and no signature. The onboarding document was sent and explained; no welcome email or Skool invite was mentioned at all.

objection_plays.detail: Isolation ran in substance — 'Sounds like it's just a financial constriction, basically' — and one financial-picture question ran and produced a real number: 'What do you have on hand now so we can at least get you started?' ($4,000). The break-it-up move ran, repeatedly. Never asked: monthly surplus, credit cards, available credit, used versus available, or investments. The rep also never established that the $4,000 was already spoken for until the prospect volunteered it — 'that's just like my free cash' — and only later disclosed the rent and hotel commitments that made it unavailable.

'Give me two weeks' and 'I have no issue putting it off for a week or two' are OD in substance. One fragment of the play ran — 'you also don't want to waste time, I think, I feel like' and 'we can be on a meeting with Trevor on Monday, and you can begin the workouts with him next week already' — which is the show-up-and-it's-handled move in embryo. None of the rest: no 'things never slow down', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', no 'the only thing you can control is right now'.

SCRIPT GAP — a payment-preference objection rather than an affordability one. The prospect could afford it and intended to pay in full; he simply wanted to do so in two weeks and said so twice in plain terms, including 'I don't need to muddle things up with split payments. It's how I like to operate.' There is no scripted guidance for this, and the improvisation went badly: the rep pressed four more times against an explicitly stated preference from a man who had just disclosed imminent rent and travel costs.

SCRIPT GAP — post-surgical clearance. Throat surgery one month prior was disclosed at 00:03:56 and was the stated reason the prospect was on the call at all. The playbook contains no step requiring the rep to establish whether a surgeon has cleared the prospect for exertion, and none was sought here before selling progressive loaded work.

notes: Excellent P4 — the root cause was found, named by the prospect, and it was genuine. P5 failed on phrasing rather than intent: four attempts at the settle question, all misunderstood, none rephrased successfully, so the price landed with no consequence behind it. The close is where this needs coaching: the rep had a willing buyer who wanted to pay $6,000 in full in two weeks and converted him into a $100 deposit with a contingent balance, after the buyer had twice said no to exactly that. Coach taking yes for an answer.
